Defending Champion Roger Black was clear in his heat with 45.88 while in the next race on the track our own Du'aine Ladejo ran a throttled back 46.50 to shade the Italian Aimar.

Another four rounds of major championship 400m running in two days may just have stretched Du'aine Ladejo too far after Helsinki. He looked so comfortable with 47.90, 46.26 and 45.23 as he progressed to the final but a certain cool customer from Kenya had yet to show his hand.

Day two and more Belgrave action came from John Regis and Du'aine Ladejo. 1991 World Champ. USA's Antonio Pettigrew suddenly brought his 1994 season to life and coming out of the last turn he was 2 metres clear of Ladejo and in no mood to relinquish a single centimetre.

Du'aine Ladejo just had the edge as favourite after the first two rounds of the 400 metres having set the fastest heat time of 46.50 and then running 1/100th faster than Roger Black in the semis with 45.82.
